headline: Highest risk is B data leakage: EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API exposure, while awesome-prompts is a docs-only prompt repository with no isolation or provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing prompt repository with no runnable surface or I/O, while B is an email-scheduling system with HTTP API and broad egress. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or operator reuse of prompt text, so direct injection is limited. Because neither profile shows a shared channel, the interaction is weakly evidenced.
conditions: IF an operator copies A's prompt text into B's HTTP API inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF B begins parsing A-authored content as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Do not paste untrusted prompt text into B inputs.
Add a manual review step before any B action.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B touches IoT data and has broad egress plus an HTTP API. If A and B share a workspace or operator context, B can leak whatever content is introduced into it. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, though not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF A content is placed into B's HTTP API payloads, B can transmit it off-host.
IF A and B share an OS workspace, B may ingest files or notes containing sensitive material.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared workspace.
Restrict B's API inputs to non-sensitive test data.
Disable or firewall B egress during review.
Separate operator accounts for A and B.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces, while B exposes an HTTP API but no filesystem, git, or OAuth write scopes. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so capability conflict is limited to unusual orchestration mistakes. Uncertainty is low because A lacks operational capabilities entirely.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps A's outputs into B's mutable API state, conflicts can occur.
IF both agents are given the same downstream resource outside these profiles, write contention may emerge.
mitigations: Avoid assigning both agents the same mutable target.
Use read-only inputs for A.
Serialize any B API writes.
Document ownership of each resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces prompt content and B is an email-scheduling system with an HTTP API, so A's output could be treated as authoritative input by B or an operator. No verification mechanism is shown in either profile, and B has downstream action potential. This is a default-use cascade risk, though not directly evidenced as automated.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as scheduling instructions without review, erroneous actions can propagate.
IF an operator trusts A's prompt recommendations as facts, B may execute bad downstream actions.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output.
Limit B to draft-only mode.
Add a checklist for factual verification.
Log A-to-B handoffs for audit.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for B inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source prompt repository with no touched data classes, while B touches IoT data and has broad egress. The profiles do not show residency, retention, or certification mismatches, so a compliance breach is not established. The only cited concern is that B handles IoT data, which could become regulated if paired with sensitive inputs.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is routed through B, compliance review becomes necessary.
IF A is used to generate content containing restricted data, retention policy review is needed.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data into B.
Review retention settings for B.
Keep A content free of personal data.
Record data-class ownership for each workflow.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
